title: Hildegard's music
hook: she wrote music still sung, including a sung drama of the virtues where only the devil can't sing
tomorrow: keep each poet's name on the line, or blend them all like honey?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: greening. Hildegard's word for God's life rising in plants, bodies and souls, with dryness as its opposite. Now the sound she made of it.

In a lot of musicals the villain gets the best song. Hildegard did the opposite. She wrote a sung drama called the Ordo Virtutum, the Play of the Virtues. A human soul is pulled between the Virtues and the Devil, wanders off with him, and comes back wounded, and the Virtues welcome her home. Every part in it is sung, the soul, the Virtues, all of them. Except one. The Devil never gets a single note. He only shouts. Why would a composer take the music away from her villain?
screen: `THE VILLAIN USUALLY GETS THE BEST SONG.` → `A SOUL BETWEEN VIRTUES AND DEVIL.` → `EVERY PART IS SUNG.` → `THE DEVIL ONLY SHOUTS.`

segments.voice: Her answer shows up in a fight late in her life. Hildegard's community buried a young nobleman who had once been excommunicated. She said he had been reconciled before he died. Church officials in Mainz ordered the body dug up. She refused. So her whole house was put under an interdict: no Mass, and no singing. The nuns could only say their prayers quietly. Hildegard wrote the officials a letter, and it's really a teaching on music. Before the fall, she says, Adam's voice joined the praise of the angels. Music is how people remember that lost harmony, and how they join it again. The Devil, she writes, hates that sound, and works to silence it. So anyone who silences praise without good cause should ask whose work they're doing. There's the answer to the puzzle. For Hildegard, singing God's praise isn't decoration. It's heaven's harmony, the thing the Devil walked away from. He can shout. He can't sing. The same conviction runs through her Benedictine world, where monks and nuns sang their prayers through the day instead of only saying them. In time the ban was lifted and her nuns sang again. And her songs are still sung by choirs and monastic communities. If a piece of music has ever sounded like a memory of somewhere you've never been, Hildegard would call it a memory of paradise.
screen: `A BURIAL, AND AN ORDER TO DIG.` · `NO MASS. NO SINGING.` · `MUSIC: A MEMORY OF PARADISE.` · `THE DEVIL CAN'T SING.` · then, large: `HER MUSIC.`

segments.voice: Find a recording of one of Hildegard's chants, O viridissima virga or any other, and listen with nothing else open. If no recording is near, hum one long, low note on each out-breath and let it fill your chest.
Hildegard's music: her chants and her sung drama of the Virtues, where praise is heaven's harmony and only the Devil can't sing.
Keep this one: her music, the song Hildegard defended when praise was banned. See you tomorrow.

excommunicated.meaning: cut off from the church's sacraments as a penalty

Mainz.meaning: a German city whose church officials oversaw her community

interdict.meaning: a church ban on Mass and sacraments for a place or group

Benedictine.meaning: following the Rule of Saint Benedict, a monastic way of life
